monthly_review.summary: September shows clear acceleration in intensity and efficiency versus August, with notable shifts toward higher-zone work and improved pace — though cadence dropped slightly and aerobic TE rose modestly.
monthly_review.highlight: Pace improved by 34 sec/km while average HR increased 7 bpm and zone distribution shifted from 43% Z1 in August to only 20% Z1 in September — confirming a deliberate, sustained increase in intensity that aligns with the multi-month trend (Z1 dropped from 36% in May → 19% in July → 20% in Sept).

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already exceeded last month’s distance (66.0 vs 51.3 km) and run count (13 vs 10) with 5 days remaining — no additional running is needed to match August, and given the absence of recovery metrics, adding volume would be inadvisable without confirmation of readiness.

insights.title: Strategic shift into Z3–Z4 work
insights.body: Z3+Z4 time jumped from 34% in August (26% Z3 + 8% Z4) to 53% in September (32% Z3 + 21% Z4), coinciding with a 34 sec/km pace improvement and +7 bpm avg HR — indicating successful progression into threshold and tempo work without Z5 overload.

insights.title: Efficiency decline correlates with cadence drop and higher-intensity focus
insights.body: Avg efficiency worsened from 14.12 to 14.6 ml/kg/km while avg cadence fell from 149 to 145 spm — and stride length remained stable (76–86 cm across recent runs), suggesting reduced neuromuscular coordination or fatigue-mediated form compromise during faster efforts.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling remains well-controlled despite intensity increase
insights.body: All recent runs show aerobic TE between 2.4–3.1%, staying under the 5% decoupling threshold — confirming the aerobic system is resilient even as volume and intensity rise, likely supported by the long-term base built in prior months (e.g., 14 runs in July, 82.4 km).
